# Kali Linux

A Debian-derived distribution that ships several hundred security tools preinstalled and preconfigured.
It is the attack host for every practical lab in
[[cybersecurity-engineering-laboratories]] from lab 07 onward.

## The point of a tooling distribution

Not the tools themselves — almost all are separately installable — but that **the environment is
someone else's problem**. Package versions that work together, tools on the path, a repeatable image
you can revert. In a fourteen-lab course where each session uses a different tool
([[openssl]], [[wireshark]], [[nmap]], [[metasploit]], [[owasp-zap]], Ettercap, theHarvester,
dnsenum, netcat), the alternative is spending each session installing rather than learning.

The lab reports show the value negatively: the failures that *are* recorded are overwhelmingly
environment failures — a GUI front end that would not install, a tool erroring on invocation, a local
service that would not start — and they cluster in the labs that reach outside the preinstalled set.

## The lab range

The whole environment is VirtualBox VMs on one workstation, which is the second half of the same idea:

| VM | Role |
|---|---|
| **Kali Linux** | attacker; two instances where a lab needs both ends of a conversation |
| **Ubuntu Server** | the honest host — PKI, CA and OpenVPN work in lab 07 |
| **Metasploitable 2 / 3** | deliberately vulnerable target for MitM, recon and exploitation |
| **pfSense** | firewall/router, so scans meet a real filter |

Two Kali VMs either side of a VPN is how lab 09 gets a conversation it can capture from both sides —
see [[cia-triad]]. Snapshots are what make an exploitation lab survivable: the target is expected to
end in an unknown state.

**Virtualisation is also the containment boundary.** A self-contained virtual network with
deliberately vulnerable hosts is what makes the offensive material legal and safe to run, and it is
the concrete meaning of the repository's scope statement — 2022 coursework against targets provided
for the purpose, nothing run against a system without authorisation.

## The honest caveat

A preloaded distribution makes tools available; it does not make them understood. Reading a scan's
ambiguous port states, choosing between scan types, or knowing why a capture shows nothing are skills
the distribution does not supply. The measurable work in this repository is mostly the crypto labs,
which ran on Windows with [[cryptool]] and needed no distribution at all.
